title: Game Concepts
short_description: Game Concepts are fundamental building blocks of our software.
infobox:
This table contains all Game Concepts. By default, it is sorted from most to least recent. Game Concepts are fundamental building blocks of our software.

Relationships:
• Each Game Concept is made by exactly one Team of Type “Studio (Game Design)”. (Each Team can make any number of Game Concepts.)
• Each Game Concept can be—but is usually not—a Variant of exactly one existing other Game Concept.
• Each Game Concept can be implemented as a Game one or multiple times, as long as the Platform of the implementation differs. (Each Game is the concrete implementation of exactly one Game Concept.)

title: Games
short_description: Games are implemen­tations of Game Concepts for different Platforms.
infobox:
This table contains all Games. By default, it is sorted from most to least recent. Games are implemen­tations of Game Concepts for different Platforms.

Relationships:
• Each Game is the concrete implementation of exactly one Game Concept. (Each Game Concept can be implemented as a Game one or multiple times, as long as the Platform of the implementation differs.)
• Each Game is first contained in exactly one Version. (Each Version can contain any number of new Games.)
• Optionally, a Version can be specified where the Game has been removed, ending the chain of inheritance.
• Specify Game Reuses for additional uses of the Game outside of the original chain of inheritance.

title: Game Reuses
short_description: Game Reuses inject Games into additional Versions (same Platform).
infobox:
This table contains all Game Reuses. By default, it is sorted from most to least recent. Game Reuses inject Games into additional Versions (same Platform). Use Game Reuses to specify additional uses of the Game outside of the original chain of inheritance. (Remember to specify the primary use directly in the Game.)

Relationships:
• Each Game Reuse refers to exactly one Game. (Each Game can have any number of Game Reuses, including none at all.)
• Each Game Reuse is first contained in exactly one Version. (Each Version can contain any number of Game Reuses.) — Optionally, a Version can be specified where the Game has been removed, ending the chain of inheritance.

title: Features
short_description: Features are general capabilities not pertaining to a Game.
infobox:
This table contains all Features. By default, it is sorted by Version. Features are general capabilities not pertaining to a Game.

Relationships:
• Each Feature is first contained in exactly one Version. (Each Version can contain any number of new Features.)

title: Versions
short_description: Versions bundle Games and Features into an abstract product.
infobox:
This table contains all Versions. By default, it is sorted from most to least recent. Versions bundle Games and Features into an abstract product.

Relationships:
• Each Version can Inherit from another Version to start or continue the chain of inheritance. If it does not Inherit from another Version, the Version starts a new chain of inheritance.
• Each Version can contain any number of new Games. (Each Game is first contained in exactly one Version.)
• Each Version can contain any number of new Features. (Each Feature is first contained in exactly one Version.)
• Each Version can have any number of Builds. (Each Build belongs to exactly one Version.)
• Each Version can have any number of Availabilities. (Each Availability belongs to exactly one Version.)

title: Builds
short_description: Builds make deliverable products out of abstract Versions.
infobox:
This table contains all Builds. By default, it is sorted by Version. Builds make deliverable products out of abstract Versions.

Relationships:
• Each Build belongs to exactly one Version. (Each Version can have any number of Builds.)
• Each Build is for exactly one Jurisdiction. (Each Jurisdiction can have any number of Builds.)

title: Dongles
short_description: Dongles select Games and apply Jurisdictional settings to a Version.
infobox:
This table contains all Dongles. By default, it is sorted by Name. Dongles select Games and apply Jurisdictional settings to a Version.

Relationships:
• Each Dongle applies to exactly one Version. (Each Version can have any number of Dongles.)
• Each Dongle is for exactly one Jurisdiction. (Each Jurisdiction can have any number of Dongles.)

title: Defects
short_description: Defects require a Game to be disabled entirely or within a specific scope.
infobox:
This table contains all Defects. By default, it is sorted from most to least recent. Defects usually require a Game to be disabled in a Build, Version or altogether.

Relationships:
• Each Defect belongs to exactly one Version OR to exactly one Build OR to neither. (Each Version and each Build can have any number of Defects.) — If Version and Build are both not set, the Defect applies to every occurrence of the Game. Note that it is not useful to set both Version and Build.
• Each Defect is for exactly one Game. (Each Game can have any number of Defects, as long as they are for different Versions or Builds.)

title: Ver Milestones
short_description: Ver Milestones are time-bound Statuses (target, actual) for Versions.
infobox:
This table contains all Ver Milestones. By default, it is sorted by Expected Date. Ver Milestones are time-bound Statuses (target, actual) for Versions.

Relationships:
• Each Ver Milestone applies to exactly one Version. (Each Version can have any number of Ver Milestones.)
• Each Ver Milestone applies to exactly one Jurisdiction. (Each Jurisdiction can have any number of Ver Milestones.)

title: Build Milestones
short_description: Build Milestones are time-bound Statuses (target, actual) for Builds.
infobox:
This table contains all Build Milestones. By default, it is sorted by Expected Date. Build Milestones are time-bound Statuses (target, actual) for Builds.

Relationships:
• Each Build Milestone applies to exactly one Build. (Each Build can have any number of Build Milestones.)
• Each Build Milestone applies to exactly one Jurisdiction. (Each Jurisdiction can have any number of Build Milestones.)

title: Game Milestones
short_description: Game Milestones are time-bound Statuses (target, actual) for Games.
infobox:
This table contains all Game Milestones. By default, it is sorted by Expected Date. Game Milestones are time-bound Statuses (target, actual) for Games.

Relationships:
• Each Game Milestone applies to exactly one Game. (Each Game can have any number of Game Milestones.)

infobox:

Relationships:
—

short_description: Components are used with Cabinets to create a Configuration.
infobox:
This table contains all Components. By default, it is sorted by SKU. Components are used with Cabinets to create a Configuration.

Relationships:
—

title: Configurations
short_description: Configurations combine Cabinets with Compo­nents into a deliverable product.
infobox:
This table contains all Configurations. By default, it is sorted by SKU. Configurations combine Cabinets with Compo­nents into a deliverable product.

Relationships:
—

title: Compatibilities
short_description: Compatibilities describe which Components work with which Versions.
infobox: This table contains all Compatibilities. By default, it is sorted by Version. Compatibilities describe which Components work with which Versions.

title: Availabilities
short_description: Availabilities document where Versions should not, should or can be delivered.
infobox:
This table contains all Availabilities. By default, it is sorted by Version. Availabilities document where Versions should not, should or can be delivered.

Relationships:
• Each Availability belongs to exactly one Version. (Each Version can have any number of Availabilities.)
• Each Availability is for exactly one Jurisdiction. (Each Jurisdiction can have any number of Availabilities.)

title: Installations
short_description: Installations document where Versions have been delivered, either “live” or for testing.
infobox:
This table contains all Installations. By default, it is sorted by Version. Installations document where Versions have been delivered, either “live” or for testing.

See the Installations Report for a convenient way to browse Installations.

Relationships:
• Each Installation belongs to exactly one Version. (Each Version can have any number of Installations.)
• Each Installation is for exactly one Jurisdiction. (Each Jurisdiction can have any number of Installations.)
default_view_columns: version_ID, jurisdiction_ID, venue_ID, live, test, planned

title: Focus Groups
short_description: Focus Groups document where Versions have been discussed with players.
infobox:
This table contains all Focus Groups. By default, it is sorted by Version. Focus Groups document where Versions have been discussed with players.

See the Focus Groups Report for a convenient way to browse Focus Groups.

Relationships:
• Each Focus Group belongs to exactly one Version. (Each Version can have any number of Focus Groups.)
• Each Focus Group is for exactly one Jurisdiction. (Each Jurisdiction can have any number of Focus Groups.)

title: Releases
short_description: Releases record market availability of a deliverable product (that is, of a Build).
infobox:
This table contains all Releases. By default, it is sorted by Release Date. Releases record market availability of a deliverable product (that is, of a Build).

Relationships:
• Each Release belongs to exactly one Build. (Each Build can have none or exactly one Release.)
• Each Release is specified with exactly one Base Dongle. (Each Dongle can be used as a Base Dongle for any number of Releases.)

title: Jurisdictions
short_description: Jurisdictions are countries, regions, market segments, and non-country specific entities.
infobox:
This table contains all Jurisdictions. By default, it is sorted by ISO-3166. Jurisdictions are countries, regions, market segments, and non-country specific entities.

Relationships:
• Each Jurisdiction can have any number of Builds. (Each Build is for exactly one Jurisdiction.)
• Each Jurisdiction can have any number of Availabilities. (Each Availability is for exactly one Jurisdiction.)
• Each Jurisdiction can have any number of Installations. (Each Installation is for exactly one Jurisdiction.)
• Each Jurisdiction can have any number of Partner Activities. (Each Partner Activity is for exactly one Jurisdiction.)
• Each Jurisdiction gets its approvals from exactly one Authority. (Each Authority can be responsible for any number of Jurisdictions.)
default_view_columns: flag, color, iso3166, segment, subsegment, name_english

title: Mkts Land-Based
short_description: Land-Based Markets describe characteristics of Jurisdictions related to land-based activities.
infobox:
This table contains all Land-Based Markets. By default, it is sorted by Jurisdiction. Land-Based Markets describe characteristics of Jurisdictions related to land-based activities.

Relationships:
• Each Land-Based Market belongs to exactly one Jurisdiction. (Each Jurisdiction can have no or exactly one Land-Based Market.)

title: Mkts Online
short_description: Online Markets describe characteristics of Jurisdictions related to online activities.
infobox:
This table contains all online Markets. By default, it is sorted by Jurisdiction. Online Markets describe characteristics of Jurisdictions related to online activities.

Relationships:
• Each Online Market belongs to exactly one Jurisdiction. (Each Jurisdiction can have no or exactly one Online Market.)

title: Partners
short_description: Partners are doing business with MERKUR.
infobox:
This table contains all Partners. By default, it is sorted by Name. Partners are doing business with MERKUR.

Relationships:
• Each Partner can manage any number of Venues. (Each Venue is managed by exactly one Partner.)

title: Venues
short_description: Venues are physical locations, such as casinos, managed by a Partner.
infobox:
This table contains all Venues. By default, it is sorted by Jurisdiction, then Name. Venues are physical locations, such as casinos, managed by a Partner.

Relationships:
• Each Venue is managed by exactly one Partner. (Each Partner can manage any number of Venues.)
• Each Venue belongs to exactly one Jurisdiction. (Each Jurisdiction can have any number of Venues.)

title: Partner Activities
short_description: Partner Activities connect Partners with Jurisdictions.
infobox:
This table contains all Partner Activities. By default, it is sorted by Jurisdiction. Partner Activities connect Partners with Jurisdictions.

Relationships:
• Each Partner can operate in any number of Jurisdictions. (Each Jurisdiction can have any number of Partners.)

title: Strat Domains
short_description: Strategic Domains are the categories Strategic Components fall into.
infobox:
This table contains all Strategic Domains. By default, it is sorted by Name. Strategic Domains are the categories Strategic Components fall into.

Relationships:
• Each Strategic Domain may contain any number of Strategic Components. (Each Strategic Component belongs to exactly one Strategic Domain.)

title: Strat Components
short_description: Strategic Components are the building blocks of Strategic Features.
infobox:
This table contains all Strategic Components. By default, it is sorted by Domain, then Name. Strategic Components are the building blocks of Strategic Features.

Relationships:
• Each Strategic Component may be used by any number of Strategic Features. (Each Strategic Feature may use any number of Strategic Components.)
• Each Strategic Component belongs to exactly one Strategic Domain. (Each Strategic Domain may contain any number of Strategic Components.)

title: Strat Features
short_description: Strategic Features bundle Strategic Components and go into a Product.
infobox:
This table contains all Strategic Features. By default, it is sorted by Name. Strategic Features bundle Strategic Components and go into a Product.

Relationships:
• Each Strategic Feature may use any number of Strategic Components. (Each Strategic Component may be used by any number of Strategic Features.)
• Each Strategic Feature can be a Variant of exactly one existing other Strategic Feature.

title: Products

• Each [CI] Product is made by exactly one [CI] Supplier. (Each [CI] Supplier can make any number of [CI] Products.)

infobox: [CI] Mkt Cfgs apply market-specific settings to [CI] Products.

title: Suppliers

infobox:
This table contains all [CI] Suppliers. By default, it is sorted by Name. [CI] Suppliers (=competitors) are doing business in markets relevant to MERKUR.

Relationships:
• Each [CI] Supplier can make any number of [CI] Products. (Each [CI] Product is made by exactly one [CI] Supplier.)

title: Teams
short_description: Teams stand in a well-defined relationship with entities and processes, depending on Type.
infobox:
This table contains all Teams, sorted by Name. Teams stand in a well-defined relationship with entities and processes, depending on Type:

• Studios (Game Design) are responsible for the mechanics, appearance and, ultimately, success of their Games.

Relationships:
• Each Team of Type “Studio (Game Design)” can make any number of Game Concepts. (Each Game Concept is made by exactly one Team.)

title: Stakes in Jdxs
short_description: Stakes in Jurisdictions (Jdxs) link stakeholders with their Jurisdictions.
infobox:
This table contains all Stakes in Jurisdictions (Jdxs). By default, it is sorted by Person (Stakeholder) and Jurisdiction. Stakes in Jurisdictions (Jdxs) link stakeholders with their Jurisdictions.

Relationships:
• Each Stake is for exactly one Person (Stakeholder). (Each Person [Stakeholder] can have multiple Stakes.)
• Each Stake is for exactly one Jurisdiction. (Each Jurisdiction can have any number of Stakes.)

title: Authorities
short_description: Authorities are entities issuing certificates for homologation in specific Jurisdictions.
infobox:
This table contains all Authorities, sorted by Name. Authorities are entities that can issue certificates for homologation in specific Jurisdictions.

Relationships:
• Each Authority can be responsible for any number of Jurisdictions. (Each Jurisdiction gets its approvals from exactly one Authority.)

title: Platforms
short_description: Platforms are used with Games.
infobox:
This table contains all Platforms, sorted by Name. Platforms are used with Games.

Relationships:
• Each Platform can be used by any number of Games. (Each Game is for exactly one Platform.)

title: Hardware Types
short_description: Hardware Types are used with Components.
infobox:
This table contains all Hardware Types, sorted by Name. Hardware Types are used with Components.

Relationships:
• Each Hardware Type can be used by any number of Components. (Each Component is of exactly one Hardware Type.)

title: Matrix Templates
short_description: Matrix Templates define the default number of rows and columns and pre-populate titles for matrices.
infobox:
This table contains all Matrix Templates, sorted by referred Table. Matrix Templates define the default number of rows and columns and pre-populate titles for matrices.

Relationships:
• Each Hardware Type can be used by any number of Components. (Each Component is of exactly one Hardware Type.)
